_note: The non-prompt half of the Retell agent, version-controlled. agent/vNN_prompt.txt covers what
the agent SAYS; this file covers everything else Retell holds that changes how a call goes —
turn-taking, tool timeouts, and which response fields reach the prompt. Both halves were
previously unreviewable, and three of Round 20's known-unfixed defects lived in this half.
`python tools/retell_suite.py config` reports drift between this file and the live agent;
`--apply` writes it. Publishing a version and re-pointing the phone number stay manual —
see agent/README.md, Publishing. Keys starting with _ are documentation and are never sent.
Every key below is placed on the object Retell actually reads it from: the six under `agent`
are AgentRequest fields (PATCH /update-agent), and timeout_ms / response_variables are
per-tool fields inside the LLM's general_tools array (PATCH /update-retell-llm). A correct
value on the wrong object is accepted and ignored, which is the quietest way to lose a fix.
IDs are read from RETELL_AGENT_ID / RETELL_LLM_ID, never stored here: this repo is public and
they identify the live phone agent.

_why.enable_backchannel: Round 20 defect. backchannel_frequency was 0.8, which fires 'mm-hmm' into the pauses between spelled letters — and the v46 name ladder's whole recovery path is asking a caller to spell their last name, then their first and last. It is the one turn-taking knob that actively breaks the ladder, so backchannels are off rather than merely rarer: at any frequency above zero the failure is only less frequent, not gone, and the v45 pace rule ('no filler, no repeating the caller back') already asks the agent not to do this in words.
_why.backchannel_frequency: Pinned to 0 as a second latch, not as the fix. Retell documents this field as 'Only applicable when enable_backchannel is true', so with backchannels off it changes nothing today. Its default is 0.8 — the exact value that broke the ladder — so leaving it unpinned means anyone who flips enable_backchannel back on in the dashboard silently restores the defect rather than getting a quiet agent. Range is [0,1]; 0 is legal.
_why.voice_speed: +15%, shipped with v45. Cuts perceived slowness without touching turn-taking. Range is [0.5,2]; Retell's default is 1.
_why.responsiveness: Deliberately NOT raised. The ladder asks callers to spell out loud, and tightening turn-taking is exactly what makes the agent talk over them. Note 0.7 is a recorded observation of the live agent, not Retell's default (which is 1) — --apply writes it either way.
_why.interruption_sensitivity: Same reasoning as responsiveness, and the same caveat: 0.6 is the observed live value, not the default of 1.
_why.end_call_after_silence_ms: Unchanged at 120s — but 'unchanged' means unchanged from what this agent was already set to, not from Retell's default, which is 600000. --apply does write this. The tool timeout moved instead — see tools._why.timeout_ms.

_why.timeout_ms: Round 20 defect: every tool sat at 120000ms, the same value as end_call_after_silence_ms, so a hung tool call and the silence timer expired together and which one won was a race — the losing outcome being a call that simply ends on a caller waiting for an answer. 120000 was nobody's choice, which is how it went unnoticed: it is Retell's documented default for timeout_ms, and nothing compares it against a silence timer set on a different object. 30s is comfortably clear of that, is inside Retell's allowed 1000–600000ms, and is above a cold-start round trip to Render; past it the tool errors, the agent says it is having trouble reaching records and transfers, which is a worse answer than a fast one and a much better one than a dead line.
_why.response_variables: Two defects here, and the first one was silent twice over. (1) NOTATION. These were written as JSONPath — `$.reason` — and Retell does not take JSONPath in this field: 'Point each variable at a field in the response using dot notation, with array indexing where needed — for example `user.name` or `data.items[0].id`.' `$.reason` asks for a field named `$` holding a field named `reason`, which no response this service returns has, so every mapping bound nothing. Nothing raises: an unresolved path yields no variable, and an unset dynamic variable renders as the literal text `{{reason}}`. The drift checker was comparing against a value that could never be correct, so `config` would have reported drift forever and `--apply` would have written fourteen dead mappings and printed success. (2) COVERAGE: `reason` and `verify_with` were absent from get_order_details altogether. What this is NOT, so the fix is not oversold: a custom tool's entire JSON response body is stringified into the LLM's context regardless of this field, so v46's `reason` branching — 'unverified' means ask for a different detail, 'locked' means stop and transfer, 'error' is the ONLY value meaning the records are really down — already reads the tool result directly and works with this field empty. response_variables exists only to bind those values as {{template}} variables for reuse later in the call. Worth getting right; it was never what the prompt's failure taxonomy stood on. Listed keys are the MINIMUM; extra keys already configured are left alone.
